 ‘Stargate SG-1’ Officially Returns With a Brand-New Release Next Month
 Richard Dean Anderson as Jack O'Neill in 'Stargate SG-1' Image via Showtime

 By  
 Rob London 
 Published Nov 9, 2026, 2:40 PM EST 
 A cinematic obsessive with the filmic palate of a starving raccoon, Rob London will watch pretty much anything once. With a mind like a steel trap, he's an endless fount of movie and TV trivia, borne from a misspent youth of watching monster movies on TV, perusing the sun-faded goods at the local video rental shop, and staining his fingers with ink from the Video Movie Guide. Areas of interest include science fiction, film noir, horror flicks , '70s disaster pictures, Bond movies, '90s action , giant robots , dinosaurs, super heroes , and the exuberantly schlocky output of Cannon Films. He also enjoys both Star Trek and Star Wars  when they're good, and maybe even more when they're bad. As a Canadian, he also has a vested interest in Canadian movies and TV shows, especially the cheesier ones dubbed "Canuxploitation."
An expert on Marvel Comics, he has also written for the Official Handbook of the Marvel Universe , and is a member of the Marvel Research Team. He can frequently be found pontificating on comic-book continuity or bemoaning the misfortunes of the Toronto Maple Leafs on his Twitter account.

 It's been a long, strange 12 months for Stargate fans. After over a decade of inactivity, a revival with series veteran Martin Gero at the helm was announced to much fanfare a year ago. Several months later, that revival was cancelled, only for a new take to be greenlit, this time headed up by WandaVision and Agatha All Along creator Jac Schaeffer . However, despite the rollercoaster ride of announcements and cancellations, the fan community has been well-served with collectibles, and there's one last release coming next month, just in time for Christmas.

 Stargate began in 1994 with the movie of the same name, which was written by 1990s blockbuster dream team Dean Devlin and Roland Emmerich , and directed by the latter. It centers around a US military team, led by career soldier Colonel Jack O'Neill ( Kurt Russell ) and eccentric scientist Dr. Daniel Jackson ( James Spader ), who use an ancient stargate to travel to an alien planet where an alien "god" rules over the enslaved human population. The movie was a hit, and spawned a TV spinoff, Stargate SG-1 , which ran for 10 seasons and over 200 episodes. Two SG-1 spin-offs, Stargate Atlantis and Stargate Universe , followed; however, after Universe ended in 2011, the franchise has largely lain fallow.
 Now, Master Replicas , which has been busily producing Stargate starship and prop replicas for several years, is letting fans bring one of the most famous pieces of Stargate iconography home. The helmet of the fearsome Horus Guard can now decorate your desk. The desktop replica is painstakingly detailed to perfectly replicate the prop in painted polyresin, and measures just under 6 inches tall when placed on its display stand. The Horus Guard Helmet Desktop Replica will retail for $69.99 USD, and can be pre-ordered on MasterReplicas.com . It will be released in December.

 The Matrix 
 The Resistance, Zion 
 You take the red pill, you stay in Wonderland, and I show you how deep the rabbit hole goes. 
 You would survive The Matrix because you were never fully sold on the version of reality you were handed. You notice the seams. You ask the second question. In a world built to keep people comfortable and incurious, that instinct is the whole fight, and it is why Morpheus would have found you long before you found him.

 Oh, what a day. What a lovely day. 
 You would survive the Wasteland because you do not waste energy mourning the world that ended. You move, you improvise, and you are very good with whatever is bolted to the thing in front of you. Furiosa would let you drive. That is not a compliment anybody earns easily.

 Blade Runner 
 Los Angeles, 2049 
 All those moments will be lost in time, like tears in rain. 
 You would survive 2049 because you know how to be small in a very loud city. You keep your head down, you do the job, and you hold onto one private thing that belongs only to you. That quiet stubbornness is exactly what both Deckard and K run on, and it is what keeps either of them going when the case stops making sense.

 Dune 
 Arrakis 
 Fear is the mind-killer. Fear is the little-death that brings total obliteration. 
 You would survive Arrakis because you think in decades while everyone around you thinks in weeks. You read the room, you learn the customs, you wait. The desert does not reward speed. It rewards people who understand that patience is a weapon, which is the one lesson the Fremen never had to be taught.

 Rebellions are built on hope. 
 You would survive the galaxy because you never try to survive it alone. You collect people. You end up in the middle of other folks' problems and you stay anyway. Every version of this story, from the Falcon's crew to the Ghost's, runs on somebody exactly like that holding the group together.

 Who Are the Horus Guards?
 Close The Horus Guard Desktop Replica from Stargate SG-1. Image via Master Replicas 
 The Horus Guard Desktop Replica from Stargate SG-1. Image via Master Replicas 
 The Horus Guard Desktop Replica from Stargate SG-1. Image via Master Replicas 
 The Horus Guard Desktop Replica from Stargate SG-1. Image via Master Replicas 
 First appearing in 1994's Stargate , the Horus Guards are the elite troopers of Ra, a parasitic Goa'uld alien occupying a human host and claiming to be a living god. Like the falcon-headed Egyptian god they take their name from, the Horus Guards have a bird-like, sharp beaked appearance, thanks to their distinctive helmets. They are members of the Jaffa, a genetically engineered humanoid slave race with superhuman strength and endurance. After Ra's death at the hands of the SG-1 team, they served his mate, Hathor, and their son, Heru'ur.
 The Stargate SG-1 Horus Guard Helmet from Master Replicas will be released in December. Stay tuned to Collider for future updates.
